title: U.S. Senate · Michigan

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Gary Peters did not seek re-election, making this an open seat. Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic primary and Mike Rogers ran unopposed for the Republican nomination in the August 4, 2026 primary.
Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election a Toss-up as of September 2026; Decision Desk rated it Lean Democratic.

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.currentRole: Physician and epidemiologist; former director and health officer, Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services (2022–2025)

summary.text: Abdul El-Sayed is a physician and epidemiologist who became Detroit's health director in 2015, ran for governor in 2018 and led the Wayne County health department from 2023 to 2025. He is the Democratic nominee for the open seat after winning the August 4, 2026 primary over Rep. Haley Stevens. His campaign website describes him as a public official who rebuilt health agencies and says he is running to make life in Michigan less expensive.

background.text: Born October 31, 1984, in Rochester Hills, Michigan, to Egyptian immigrant parents and raised in the Detroit area; he graduated from Bloomfield Hills Andover High School in 2003.

Earned a B.S. in biology and political science from the University of Michigan (2007), a D.Phil. in public health from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar (2011), and an M.D. from Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (2014).
Joined the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health faculty in 2014 as an assistant professor of epidemiology.

Appointed Health Officer and Executive Director of the Detroit Health Department in August 2015 by Mayor Mike Duggan to rebuild the department after the city's bankruptcy; he left in February 2017 to run for governor.
Lost the August 7, 2018 Democratic primary for governor to Gretchen Whitmer, receiving about 30% of the vote; founded the political action committee Southpaw Michigan in 2018.

Served on the Joe Biden-Bernie Sanders Unity Task Force on healthcare in 2020 and has hosted the podcast America Dissected since 2019. His campaign site says he wrote Medicare for All: A Citizen's Guide.

Named director of Wayne County's Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services in December 2022, took the role in March 2023 and resigned in April 2025 to run for the Senate; Ballotpedia lists his tenure as 2022 to 2025.

Entered the 2026 Senate race in April 2025 after Sen. Gary Peters announced he would not run again, and won the August 4 Democratic primary with 48.5% to Haley Stevens' 47.5%, with Mallory McMorrow, who had withdrawn, receiving 4.0%.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Ann Arbor with his wife, Sarah, and their two daughters.

priorities.text: Enacting Medicare for All and eliminating medical debt nationwide.

positions.quote: I literally wrote the book on Medicare for All because healthcare is a human right, not a privilege. ... I will sponsor legislation to enact M4A and eliminate medical debt nationwide. M4A guarantees comprehensive coverage, eliminates co-pays and deductibles, and lowers overall costs through reducing administrative waste and negotiating drug prices.

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed for the Republican nomination

summary.text: Mike Rogers is a former U.S. Army officer and FBI special agent who served in the Michigan Senate and then in the U.S. House for Michigan's 8th District from 2001 to 2015, where he chaired the House Intelligence Committee. After leaving Congress he worked in cybersecurity and media. He was the Republican nominee for Senate in 2024, losing narrowly to Elissa Slotkin, and is the 2026 Republican nominee.

background.text: Born June 2, 1963; his family settled in Brighton Township, and he graduated from Howell High School (Wikipedia says 1981). Ballotpedia and Wikipedia differ on his birthplace (Livingston County and Livonia, respectively).
Earned a B.S. from Adrian College in 1985 (Wikipedia says in criminal justice and sociology).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 1989.
Worked as an FBI special agent in the Chicago field office from 1989 to 1994, specializing in organized crime and public corruption.

Elected to the Michigan Senate in 1994 and re-elected in 1998, representing District 26 (Clinton, Livingston and Shiawassee counties); he was the primary sponsor of the law creating the Michigan Education Savings Program.
Won Michigan's 8th Congressional District in 2000 by 111 votes over Democratic state Sen. Dianne Byrum and served until 2015, announcing in March 2014 that he would not seek an eighth term.

In the House, served on the Energy and Commerce Committee and chaired the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence from 2011 to 2015; he introduced the Cyber Intelligence Sharing and Protection Act in 2011.

After Congress, worked in the cybersecurity industry, joined CNN as a national security commentator and hosted radio and television programs; he served on the Mitre Corporation board from 2016 to 2023, as chairman from 2021.
Announced a 2024 Senate run in August 2023, won that Republican primary, and lost the general election to Elissa Slotkin by fewer than 20,000 votes.
Announced his 2026 Senate candidacy on April 14, 2025, and won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

priorities.text: Bringing manufacturing jobs back to the U.S. and lowering the cost of gas, groceries, and prescription drugs.
Protecting Social Security and Medicare for seniors.

candidates.researchNotes: Rogers's campaign site (mikerogers.com) is JavaScript-rendered and its issue pages (healthcare plan, housing plan) did not return readable text via direct fetch, so specific issue positions beyond the quoted priority statement in Ballotpedia's race summary could not be documented from primary sources within the time available.

candidates.name: Douglas P. Marsh

summary.text: Douglas P. Marsh is the Green Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, a journalist from northern Michigan and a volunteer firefighter. He was also the Green nominee in 2024. According to his Ballotpedia survey, his campaign calls for affordable healthcare, an end to illegal wars and housing policy reform.

background.text: Born in Traverse City, Michigan, in 1984, and graduated from Elk Rapids High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in philosophy from the University of Michigan in 2006.

Worked in restaurants, ski resorts, construction and landscaping, and as an educator; according to his survey, he moved abroad in 2013 and lectured at a university in Thailand for five years before returning to the United States in 2018.
Entered community journalism in 2021 and began volunteer firefighting the following year, according to his survey.
Ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 as the Green Party candidate, receiving 1.0% (53,978 votes) in the race won by Elissa Slotkin.
Advanced from the Green Party convention on February 21, 2026. He describes himself as a husband and father.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or detailed public record found beyond Ballotpedia's listing within the time available for this research.

candidates.name: Lydia Christensen

summary.text: Lydia Christensen is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan. Ballotpedia lists her profession as CEO, and she describes herself as a computer scientist who founded her own company. According to her survey, her campaign emphasizes constitutional and digital rights, renewable energy and a Medicaid-for-all proposal.

background.text: Graduated from Appleton West High School (Wisconsin) and attended the University of Wisconsin, Oshkosh and Fox Valley Technical College.
Describes herself as trained as a computer scientist who started her own company, IronFortress LLC; Ballotpedia lists her profession as CEO.
Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on June 28, 2026.
Describes herself in her survey as a transgender candidate who enjoys music and natural environments.

candidates.name: Timothy Long

summary.text: Timothy Long is the U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan. Little public information about him was found; he has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 survey.

background.text: Ran for Wayne County Commission District 14 in 2024 as the U.S. Taxpayers Party candidate, receiving 14.3% (6,513 votes) in a race won by incumbent Alex Garza.
Advanced from the U.S. Taxpayers Party convention in July 2026 to the Senate ballot.
